reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the speaker promotes a BitClub mining-share offer with stated expected daily profits and directs viewers to pay Bitcoin to obtain a share. A sampled BitClub page shows a QR-code invoice and countdown linked to that requested transfer. The presentation is instructional and promotional, not reporting or criticizing the offer; although a page displays “Payment Received,” the records do not establish whether the transaction was caused by the offer or whether promised profits were delivered.

opening.argument: The presentation uses prospective, limited language rather than stating a quantified or guaranteed investment return. The speaker describes an example using the smallest pool and says the share will become active after ten days, while the later earnings statement gives no amount, rate, or guaranteed total. The separate $99 membership and $500 package are presented as disclosed prices, allowing viewers to understand the payment terms before proceeding.

citations.quote: I'm going to show you an example with the smallest pool, which we recommend for the start to check out the whole thing.
you need the 99 dollars one time and you need the 500 dollars for the smallest pack
it's going to be ten days from which my mining share is going to be active
from that moment you're going to earn daily profits out of your bitcoin mind share

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats the words “daily profits” as conclusive proof of a scam, but that phrase identifies the expected function of the purchased mining share; it does not establish that the speaker guaranteed a particular return or concealed the price. The payment sequence is openly described as a Bitcoin purchase with a stated fee, and the record itself does not establish that any promised earnings were actually delivered.

citations.quote: I know my $500 fee costs me 1699 bitcoin.
from that moment you're going to earn daily profits out of your bitcoin mind share

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling the statement prospective does not make it a neutral warning: the speaker directly tells viewers that, after activation, they will earn daily profits. The video also instructs viewers to pay $99 and $500 for the membership and mining package. Whether a precise amount was stated is immaterial to the promotional promise of recurring profit after payment.

citations.quote: you need the 99 dollars one time and you need the 500 dollars for the smallest pack
from that moment you're going to earn daily profits out of your bitcoin mind share

opening.argument: The video's central activity is an operational walkthrough: it explains how to set up an account, create an e-wallet, buy Bitcoin, copy a payment address, and complete a transaction. Its title expressly describes setup and upgrade of an account and e-wallet, and the speaker repeatedly says he is showing viewers how the process works. The sampled footage is also presented as a screen demonstration, including a Hangouts On Air presentation and recursive screen-sharing view. That instructional format supports treating the content as technology and payment education, not as proof that viewers should trust an investment.

citations.quote: How to setup and upgrade your BitClub Network account & E-Wallet
i'm going to show you now how you will set up your BitClub network account
When we come on the starting page it might look like this.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's own description confirms the video is instructional: it says the speaker demonstrates buying a mining share and walks through the payment. Showing viewers how an online wallet and Bitcoin transfer operate is not itself deception. A countdown and QR code show the mechanics of an invoice, but they do not prove that the demonstration was fabricated or that the speaker made an independently verified claim about results.

citations.quote: i'm going to show you right now in this process how I'm going to finally buy my mining pool share
we have 10 minutes of time, a window, to make this payment

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The tutorial format does not neutralize what the tutorial teaches. This is not merely wallet education: the operational steps culminate in buying a BitClub mining share, followed by the claim that the purchaser will earn daily profits. The title and screen recording establish presentation format, but they do not show independent testing, criticism, or a warning about the offer.

citations.quote: i'm going to show you right now in this process how I'm going to finally buy my mining pool share
from that moment you're going to earn daily profits out of your bitcoin mind share
How to setup and upgrade your BitClub Network account & E-Wallet

opening.argument: The observable transaction is structured like a disclosed purchase of a service: the speaker identifies a one-time membership fee, identifies the smallest pool price, selects Bitcoin as the payment method, and shows an invoice with a QR code and countdown. The sampled pages show an ordinary account, wallet, exchange, and payment workflow. They do not show a downline, recruitment commission, credential request, or separate deposit mechanism. The presence of a future service claim should not by itself certify the external service as fraudulent.

citations.quote: you need the 99 dollars one time and you need the 500 dollars for the smallest pack
The payment has to be done in Bitcoin right now

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution identifies a purchase and a future earnings statement, but those facts are also consistent with a paid service whose performance is not established by this recording. The invoice page and payment confirmation document a transaction flow, not a hidden deposit or downline structure. Even the prosecution concedes that the displayed payment does not establish whether promised profits were delivered.

citations.quote: And That's it. That's all you need to do to make a payment possible
But finally in 10 days it will be starting and from them you can see daily Profit earnings appear from my mining earnings

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A disclosed price does not make the offer ordinary commerce when the purchase is tied to promised recurring profits. The speaker directs viewers to buy the smallest mining package, pay Bitcoin to the supplied address, and then says daily profit earnings will appear. The absence of a downline or credential request is irrelevant because the relevant mechanism is payment for a mining share and promised returns.
